# Leader standard work

A leader's own daily routine, in the same steps/key-points/reasons shape as a work instruction — what keeps a KPI tree, a training matrix, and a kaizen event's gains from quietly decaying once the excitement wears off.

Family: Daily management · Format: .xlsx · Domain: core

## What it is

Leader standard work is a work instruction for the leader's own job: the specific daily or weekly checks that keep a team's systems actually running instead of becoming paperwork nobody looks at. Same shape as any other work instruction — major steps, each with a key point for how to do it right and the reason it matters — applied to a leadership routine instead of a frontline task.

## When to use it

Use it when:

- You've built a KPI tree, a training matrix, or a daily/escalation process and want to make sure someone actually checks it, not just that it exists.
- A team lead role is changing hands and you want the new leader doing the same real routine as the last one, not reinventing it from memory.
- You want to see honestly which parts of the routine still have no real technique behind them.

Not when:

- The role is too new or too undefined to have a real routine yet — run it informally first, then document what actually works.
- You're documenting what a leader should ideally do in theory rather than what a real routine looks like — start from what's actually happening.

## How to fill it in

- **purpose** — What does this routine accomplish, and what would drift or decay without it?
- **steps** — Drafted from your description of the routine — major steps, each with zero or more key points and, for every key point, the reason it matters.
- **narrative** — Drafted from the steps actually built.

## What good looks like

The example below is the queue lead's own daily routine for the renewal-risk support process running through this catalogue's other examples — checking the KPI tree, walking the queue against the ILUO matrix's real coverage, confirming on-call. This is literally what keeps those other artifacts alive day to day, not a separate exercise.

Full worked example, on-screen and as a downloadable .xlsx: https://katafacts.com/katas/leader-standard-work

## Common mistakes

- **Writing a routine that's really just a restated job description.** — Leader standard work is a specific, repeatable checklist of real checks — a job description doesn't tell tomorrow's leader what to actually do at 9am.
- **Treating the routine as done once it's written, never revisited.** — The whole point is catching drift before it becomes a real problem — a leader standard work document that's never updated is exactly the paperwork it exists to prevent.

## What it connects to

Downstream:

- **KPI tree** — A leader standard work routine is often literally 'check the KPI tree' as its first step — the routine is what makes the tree get looked at.
- **ILUO training matrix** — Walking a queue against real training coverage, not just who's assigned, is a leader standard work step that uses the ILUO matrix directly.

## Where AI helps

Judgement — stays with you:

- Deciding what actually needs daily leader attention versus what can run on its own
- Deciding whether a drafted key point reflects real technique or is worth sharpening

Analysis — AI helps:

- Drafting major steps, key points, and reasons from a description of the routine
- Drafting the narrative from the steps actually built

Drudgery — automated:

- Counting steps and key points
- Identifying which steps still have no key point
- Exporting to xlsx in the house format
